Chemotherapy therapies work by targeting rapidly dividing cells, to stop the proliferation of cancer cells. The unintended consequence of chemotherapy is its effect on various cell types that also rapidly divide. Hair follicle cells are among them. As hair growth is a continuous cycle of cell division, chemotherapy can damage these cells. This leads to hair loss during or after treatment. However, chemotherapy is a vital tool against cancer, often extending the life expectancy of patients.

Chemo therapy is often misunderstood. Chemo involves creating psychosis in the medicinal view, and the absence of head hair is more often than not temporary. The hair growth cycle is influenced by hormones, which chemotherapy impacts. The end objective of using chemo is not to make patients bald so there can be a sale of hair growth drugs but rather to destroy cancer cells. Chemotherapy kills both healthy cells and unhealthy cells. Pain is mitigated by using various forms of medication to help manage side effects. Most hair loss is temporary and often returns. It is not a permanent side effect and in some men balding can be a long term side effect due to hormonal changes brought about by chemotherapy in men.
